changes.after: ['と','with: another participant','友達と話します。']
changes.reason: This example teaches the conversation partner, not quotation. The quotation use has its own ～と言う row.

changes.before: ['～ことがある','experience','日本へ行ったことがあります。']
changes.after: ['～ことがある','past experience: verb ta-form + ことがある','日本へ行ったことがあります。']
changes.reason: Past experience requires the past verb form. Dictionary-form verb + ことがある instead means something happens sometimes. Keeping the historical label avoids invalidating saved answer labels.

changes.before: ['～そうです','looks like / I heard','雨が降りそうです。']
changes.after: ['～そうです','appearance: looks likely to','雨が降りそうです。']
changes.reason: 降りそう uses the verb stem for appearance. Hearsay is 降るそう with a plain clause; combining the English glosses hides a real construction difference.

changes.after: ['～はずです','expected to: inference based on known facts'
changes.reason: Separate epistemic expectation from an obligation.

changes.before: ['～ばかり','nothing but / just did','彼はゲームばかりしています。']
changes.after: ['～ばかり','nothing but: repeated focus on a thing','彼はゲームばかりしています。']
changes.reason: This noun + ばかり example does not teach plain-past + ばかり, which means just did. The full note explains the difference.

changes.before: ['～上で','upon / in doing','内容を確認した上で署名してください。']
changes.after: ['～上で','after first completing a necessary step','内容を確認した上で署名してください。']
changes.reason: The exact example uses plain past + 上で for a prerequisite sequence; dictionary-form + 上で has a different in-doing use.
